wave: VERIFICATION BLINDNESS -- the sole existing test for parse_repo_manifest asserted only that its output passes validate_manifest, a materially weaker property than the test's own name promises, since validate_manifest never checks manifest.repo and only checks the four root-array fields for containment, never for matching the parsed TOML content
wave_title: Eighteenth generation this cycle. After several consecutive honest negative results in isolated-code-bug hunting (a hash-collision-pattern sweep of every stable_id call site, a full read of core/src/graph/mod.rs and runtime/src/census/extraction.rs), pivoted to a different investigative angle explicitly named in the standing priority order: verification blindness -- auditing whether EXISTING tests actually verify what their names claim, rather than hunting for new code bugs. Found a real, previously-unnoticed gap in the only test covering parse_repo_manifest.
priority_classification: verification blindness -- a distinct category in the standing priority order from correctness/security. Not a live production bug (parse_repo_manifest's current field assignments are correct), but a real gap in this project's own verification coverage: the sole test for this function would not catch a plausible, easy-to-introduce future regression (a copy/paste field swap), silently passing even though the parser's behavior would be materially wrong.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to auditing existing tests (not this cycle's own newly-added ones) for tautological or weaker-than-claimed assertions across a sample of files not yet extensively covered this cycle. Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read parse_repo_manifest's real, current implementation directly (confirmed backend_roots/frontend_roots are currently correctly assigned, not already swapped), read validate_manifest's real implementation directly (confirmed it checks only 8 scalar fields for exact equality against hardcoded constants, plus containment-only checks on the four root-array fields, and never touches manifest.repo at all), and confirmed via grep that parse_repo_manifest has exactly one test anywhere in the workspace.
key_finding: parses_atlas_manifest_policy_fields's only assertion was `assert!(validate_manifest(&manifest).is_empty())` -- proving the parsed manifest passes POLICY VALIDATION, not that PARSING itself is correct. validate_manifest never reads manifest.repo, and for source_roots/backend_roots/frontend_roots/test_roots it only verifies each declared path is lexically contained within the repository root (declared_root_is_contained) -- never that the parsed value equals what the TOML fixture actually declared. A real, plausible bug (backend_roots and frontend_roots accidentally swapped in parse_repo_manifest's own field list -- an easy copy/paste slip, since the four array! macro invocations building these fields are visually near-identical) would leave both swapped values as ordinary, non-escaping relative paths, so validate_manifest would still report zero violations and this test would still pass, even though the parser now silently misattributes which paths are backend vs. frontend roots -- a real, load-bearing distinction this manifest format exists to declare.
verification_before_acting: Read parse_repo_manifest's real, current implementation directly, confirming the four array! calls for source_roots/backend_roots/frontend_roots/test_roots and that their key arguments are currently correctly matched to their field names (not already swapped) -- this is a test-strengthening generation, not a live-bug fix, and confirming the absence of a live bug was necessary before deciding the right response was strengthening the test rather than fixing production code.

Read validate_manifest's real implementation directly, confirming exactly which fields it checks (8 scalar fields via exact-equality, 4 boolean fields via required-true, the four root-array fields via containment-only) and confirming manifest.repo is never referenced anywhere in it.

Grepped the whole workspace for parse_repo_manifest to confirm parses_atlas_manifest_policy_fields is genuinely the only test exercising it -- not one of several tests where another might already cover the gap.

Independently reconstructed the exact swap-bug scenario the survey described and injected it into the real production code to directly observe whether the pre-existing test assertion (validate_manifest(&manifest).is_empty()) would catch it, before writing or trusting the strengthened test.

design_decisions.question: Fix production code, or strengthen the test?
design_decisions.decision: Strengthen the test only. parse_repo_manifest's current field assignments are correct today (independently confirmed by reading the real code); the gap is in verification coverage, not in current behavior. Strengthening the existing test to assert directly on the parsed struct's own field values (manifest.repo, source_roots, backend_roots, frontend_roots, test_roots) closes the gap without touching production code that isn't actually broken.

design_decisions.question: How to falsify a test-strengthening change, given there is no production bug to revert-and-confirm against?
design_decisions.decision: Inverted the usual falsification direction: instead of reverting a fix and confirming a test fails, temporarily INJECTED the exact described bug (swapping backend_roots/frontend_roots's array! key arguments) into production code, confirmed the strengthened test's new assertions catch it (while the pre-existing validate_manifest assertion alone does not), then reverted the injected bug -- proving both halves of the claim directly: the old test was blind to this bug, and the new test is not.
